transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-21
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Noah Park (Redwood CSM), Priya Patel (SignalWorks Head of Security), Carlos Mendes (SignalWorks Platform Eng), Aisha Khan (Product), Tom Becker (Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick alignment on security gating items for pilot continuation. Confirm what evidence SignalWorks needs for internal auditors and legal; decide log forwarding and retention windows; schedule on-prem connectivity test.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): okay everyone, thanks for joining, do we have audio okay?
[00:08] Priya (SignalWorks): yeah we're good, thanks.
[00:12] Maya: i'll kick us off — this is week two of the pilot check-in focused specifically on governance, so sso, audit logs, retention, soc2 questions. liam will run through the infra side and Noah will cover any success metrics.
[00:28] Liam (Redwood SE): hi all, quick context — we've been running the Dedicated instance in the staging vpc you shared, kv cache traces look normal, there's a small spike in tail latency when batch size auto-increases, i have notes.
[00:34] Carlos: sorry can you repeat that about the kv cache, i missed — is that the, the key value cache for context?
[00:40] Liam: yeah, kv cache for the model state, it's the prefix cache; sometimes when a lot of concurrent chat sessions hit it there's micro-bursts. not a showstopper, more tuning.
[00:52] Priya: i want to start with SSO — our security team needs confirmation it's SAML 2.0, IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows both supported, and that we can map groups to RBAC roles. also we need audit trails for admin actions.
[01:10] Maya: absolutely — Redwood supports SAML 2.0, we do both flows. mapping groups to RBAC is supported in the Console, you can map to roles like admin, observer, deployer. we will send the SAML metadata after the call.
[01:25] Tom (Legal): and on the RBAC, can you produce an export of role assignments for audit? is that in the product today?
[01:34] Noah (CSM): yes, there's an audit export — we can stream admin audit logs to S3 or push to your SIEM via syslog. export includes role changes, token creation, and important security events.
[01:46] Priya: okay, for audit forwarding — we prefer pushing to our Splunk instance, syslog over TLS if possible. does Redwood support syslog/tls?
[01:55] Liam: we do — we have a forwarder that can speak syslog/tls to customer endpoints. couple notes: we also support object-level logs to S3 with lifecycle rules. sometimes customers prefer both.
[02:08] Priya: would S3 be accepted by our audit team? they usually want SIEM ingest but having raw objects is useful for forensics.
[02:16] Carlos: fwiw, our infra team would rather get a continuous stream to Splunk for real-time alerts. S3 is okay as backup.
[02:25] Maya: noted. action: we'll provide a sample syslog config and a sample S3 log layout. liam will include the field schema.
[02:33] Liam: yes, i'll add the KV/cache trace also so you can correlate requests.
[02:38] Aisha (Product): on retention, our compliance doc says we need 7 year retention for certain records, 90 days for others, and immediate deletion for PII after 30 days unless flagged. can the pilot support per-record retention?
[02:52] Priya: right — and we need a PII scrub pipeline for transcripts before longer-term storage.
[02:58] Liam: short answer: we support tiered retention via lifecycle policies in S3 exports; we also have message-level retention controls if you use our private deployment. in hosted mode we can apply redact-from-storage policies — though there are nuances depending on what you send back to us versus store in your bucket.
[03:17] Priya: nuance?
[03:18] Liam: if you route logs to an external S3 that you own, you control retention and scrub. if you rely on hosted storage within Redwood, we can set retention but audit teams sometimes prefer customer-owned buckets.
[03:30] Priya: ok we prefer customer-owned S3 buckets. security policy wants the canonical logs under our control.
[03:36] Maya: perfect — next step we'll provide docs for bucket lifecycle and encryption.
[03:40] Tom: any concerns about KMS keys and customer-managed keys? we need to use our KMS for data at rest for this pilot.
[03:48] Liam: supported — Redwood Private lets you bring your own KMS (BYOK) for encryption at rest. for Hosted/Dedicated we also support customer-managed keys for S3. i'll attach the KMS integration guide.
[03:59] Priya: great. about SOC 2 evidence — we will need the SOC 2 Type II report and a list of controls, plus any penetration test reports you have. timeline?
[04:12] Maya: we can share the SOC 2 Type II attestation. full control matrix mapping to your requirements may take a bit longer but we can provide our control descriptions and where controls are evidenced in the platform. i'll email the pack today.
[04:23] Carlos: do you have any SOC 2 exclusions for private deployments? sometimes vendors exclude connected components.
[04:29] Maya: we annotate exclusions in the report; we'll highlight which controls are in-scope for private/on-prem.
[04:34] Priya: good. on legal, tom had a few dpa concerns, like sub-processing and data residency — can we get a DPA template?
[04:42] Tom: yes, we're worried about cross-border transfers, we need to confirm data residency for logs.
[04:48] Liam: if you use customer-owned buckets in a Region, logs reside there. for cross-border we can restrict routing policies.
[04:55] Tom: ok please send the DPA template.
[04:58] Maya: action: maya to send SOC2 pack, tom to send redlines by end of next week.
[05:04] Priya: switching back to pilot metrics briefly — the latency/cost numbers you posted in the sheet, can we see how they change when you enable aggressive batching vs when retention scrubbing runs?
[05:18] Liam: yes, the table has two columns for baseline and batching-on. scrub adds small CPU time on the ingest path — if you offload scrub to your side in the bucket it's cheaper on our side.
[05:29] Carlos: could you run one test where scrub runs in-line, and one where scrub is post-ingest in S3 lifecycle? we want both numbers.
[05:37] Liam: i can schedule that this week, will include token-level cost delta and 95th percentile latency.
[05:43] Noah (CSM): we'll make sure the benchmarks map to the same prompts you ran previously so it's apples-to-apples.
[05:49] Priya: what's the expected timeframe for the on-prem connectivity test?
[05:53] Liam: we can do a smoke test within 48 hours once you provide the staging VPC egress endpoint and a test cert.
[06:01] Priya: we'll get that to you today.
[06:04] Tom: small legal question — forwarding logs to our SIEM, do you need a DPA signed before that?
[06:10] Maya: best practice is to have an MSA/DPA in place, but for a pilot we sometimes do a limited access agreement; we'll get legal involved and draft a short pilot data handling addendum.
[06:21] Aisha: one more product thing — can we tag requests with customer tenant ids so we can trace back events?
[06:28] Liam: yes, we support tenant-level metadata and you can include your own trace id. we'll include how to pass it in the API.
[06:34] Priya: circling back — the audit log schema, can you show an example now?
[06:39] Liam: sure, i'll paste a short sample in the chat — fields: timestamp, actor, action, object_type, object_id, request_id, outcome, ip, user_agent. sometimes the transcription contains model outputs but we redact model text unless you opt-in.
[06:54] Priya: redaction — we need to redact PII server-side before long term retention. does Redwood offer server-side PII masking?
[07:02] Liam: we have server-side masking options but for highest assurance customers do pre-ingest scrub on their side and we recommend storing scrubbed data in customer-owned S3. server-side masking supports pattern rules and named-entity recognition, but it's not perfect — we'll include caveats.
[07:17] Priya: okay include those caveats in the security pack.
[07:21] Maya: quick check — any blockers to continue the pilot this week?
[07:25] Carlos: no blockers, just need the syslog config and the retention policy doc to finalize infra work.
[07:31] Tom: from legal, i need the DPA and any redlines; otherwise okay.
[07:36] Priya: security needs the SOC 2 pack and list of controls; otherwise go-ahead.
[07:41] Maya: great. i'll summarize next steps after the call.
[07:45] Priya: one more thing — can you provide a sample audit query that would show a role change and who approved it? our auditors like example queries.
[07:55] Liam: yes, a sample Splunk query and a raw JSON example. i'll include them in the notes.
[08:02] Aisha: timeline wise, if we close these items, when can we go to pilot evaluation?
[08:08] Noah: if docs and smoke test complete this week, the evaluation checkpoint can happen next Tuesday for a conclusive results review.
[08:16] Priya: sounds good.
[08:18] Maya: ok last part, recap of action items — liam will send syslog sample, kv traces, and run scrub vs post-ingest benchmarks; priya confirm retention windows; tom send DPA redlines; maya to send SOC2 pack and pilot data handling addendum.
[08:36] Tom: tiny nit — please timestamp when you send the SOC2 docs, we record chain of custody.
[08:40] Maya: will do. thanks everyone.
[08:43] Priya: thanks, bye.

(End of transcript)
